leaf_blight.name: Leaf Blight
leaf_blight.cause: Fungal disease, thrives in humid, wet conditions
leaf_blight.symptoms: Long grey-green or tan cigar-shaped lesions on leaves
leaf_blight.treatment: Apply a fungicide early once lesions are spotted. Rotate crops next season, avoid planting maize after maize. Clear old crop debris after harvest.

leaf_spot.name: Gray Leaf Spot
leaf_spot.cause: Fungal disease, favored by humidity and crop debris left in the field
leaf_spot.symptoms: Small rectangular tan-to-gray lesions bound by leaf veins
leaf_spot.treatment: Apply fungicide at early signs. Clear old crop debris after harvest. Rotate crops.

common_rust.name: Common Rust
common_rust.cause: Fungal disease favored by cool, humid weather
common_rust.symptoms: Small reddish-brown raised pustules scattered on both sides of leaves
common_rust.treatment: Apply fungicide if severe. Usually manageable with resistant varieties and good spacing for airflow.

streak_virus.name: Maize Streak Virus
streak_virus.cause: Spread by leafhopper insects, common after leafhoppers move from grass to young maize
streak_virus.symptoms: Pale yellow streaks running along the leaf veins, stunted growth
streak_virus.treatment: No chemical cure once infected. Control leafhopper vector with imidacloprid-based insecticide. Remove and destroy infected plants early to stop spread. Plant resistant maize varieties next season.

fall_armyworm.name: Fall Armyworm
fall_armyworm.cause: Pest — caterpillar that feeds on leaves and burrows into the whorl, invasive to Africa since 2016
fall_armyworm.symptoms: Ragged holes in leaves, window-like clear patches from small caterpillars, sawdust-like droppings in the whorl
fall_armyworm.treatment: Apply insecticide directly into the whorl in early morning or evening. Check plants regularly, catch it early before it burrows deep into the stalk.

grasshopper.name: Grasshopper damage
grasshopper.cause: Pest — grasshoppers feeding directly on leaf tissue
grasshopper.symptoms: Irregular chewed edges on leaves, sometimes entire leaves stripped in heavy infestations
grasshopper.treatment: Apply insecticide if infestation is heavy. Light infestations often don't need chemical control. Removing nearby tall grass can reduce grasshopper populations.

leaf_beetle.name: Leaf Beetle damage
leaf_beetle.cause: Pest — beetles feeding on leaf surface and tissue
leaf_beetle.symptoms: Small round or irregular holes scattered across the leaf, skeletonized patches where only veins remain
leaf_beetle.treatment: Apply insecticide if damage is spreading. Monitor regularly during early growth stages when plants are most vulnerable.

healthy.name: Healthy
healthy.symptoms: Normal green leaf color, no lesions, no visible pest damage
healthy.treatment: No treatment needed. Continue regular monitoring and good field hygiene to keep it this way.
